seo.title: Worldcoin - Global Identity Protocol
seo.description: Worldcoin provides proof-of-personhood through World ID. Verify you're human while preserving privacy using zero-knowledge proofs.
seo.keywords: Worldcoin, World ID, WLD token, proof of personhood, Orb, biometric identity

overview:
Worldcoin is building a global identity and financial network. Its core innovation is World ID—a privacy-preserving proof that you're a unique human, verified through iris scans at Orb devices.

World ID uses zero-knowledge proofs so apps can verify you're human without knowing who you are. This enables sybil-resistant airdrops, voting, and services while protecting privacy.

The WLD token is distributed to verified humans as a form of universal basic income experiment. Worldcoin runs on its own L2 (World Chain) built on Optimism technology.

1.question: What is proof of personhood?
1.answer: Proof of personhood verifies you're a unique human without revealing identity. World ID uses iris scans to create a unique hash. Apps verify you haven't registered twice. It solves the sybil problem.

2.question: Is iris scanning safe?
2.answer: Worldcoin claims iris images are deleted after creating the hash. The hash can't reverse to your iris. Privacy concerns remain valid—you're trusting their process. Regulatory scrutiny varies by country.

3.question: What is World Chain?
3.answer: World Chain is Worldcoin's L2 blockchain built on Optimism stack. It prioritizes verified humans for block space. Designed for identity-based applications. Launched in 2024.

4.question: How do I get WLD tokens?
4.answer: Get verified at an Orb (physical device in many cities). Once verified, claim WLD grants through World App. Grants are distributed periodically. Availability varies by jurisdiction.

5.question: What are the controversies?
5.answer: Concerns include: biometric data collection, Sam Altman (OpenAI) involvement, developing country targeting, centralized Orb hardware. Also regulatory challenges in various countries. Research thoroughly.
